text: Binance Adds AVA, GNS, SCR and TOWNS to Monitoring Tag List Binance announced that it will add AVA, GNS, SCR and TOWNS to its Monitoring Tag list on September 4. Binance said tokens under the Monitoring Tag generally exhibit higher volatility and risk than other listed assets and are subject to closer monitoring and periodic reviews. Tokens that no longer meet Binance's listing standards may be delisted. Separately, Binance Alpha will remove MTP, BDXN, TALE, BOS, MAIGA, TIMI, SAROS, U (Union), SERAPH, RVV, AIAV, PENGUIN, ODOS and SN3 from its recommended list. Withdrawals and selling will remain available after the removal. — link

text: Fidelity: Despite Bitcoin's Strong August Rally, It Remains Unclear Whether the Bear Market Has Ended Fidelity said that despite strong gains in Bitcoin and the broader crypto market in August, it remains unclear whether the bear market has ended. Some investors are watching for a potential bottom in November 2026 based on the four-year cycle theory. The report said that an upward move following low volatility, higher volatility, crypto regulation, monetary policy, institutional adoption, and growing on-chain activity could all serve as catalysts for the market. The U.S. CLARITY Act remains under consideration in the Senate, while the SEC's proposed Regulation Crypto Assets is still in the public-comment period. — link

text: IMF: El Salvador Has Not Used Public Funds to Buy Bitcoin Since June 2025, No Further Accumulation Expected The IMF said El Salvador has provided documentation verifying that all Bitcoin accumulated since its first EFF review on June 27, 2025 came from private donations, with no public resources used. The IMF added that no further Bitcoin accumulation beyond the documented donations is expected. The disclosure came as IMF staff reached an agreement with El Salvador on the combined second and third reviews of its EFF program. Subject to IMF Executive Board approval and completion of agreed prior actions, El Salvador would gain access to approximately $140 million in additional funding. — link

text: Curve DAO appoints two Resupply developers as risk provider despite prior $9.6M exploit Curve DAO approved funding yRisk on September 2 to oversee risk management for crvUSD and Llamalend, replacing LlamaRisk, which ended its engagement early. yRisk will receive 125,000 frxUSD and 568,181 CRV through revocable one-year vesting streams. Both yRisk contributors are primary developers of Resupply, which lost approximately $9.6 million in a donation attack in June 2025; this information was not disclosed in the proposal or Curve's comparative review. In the governance vote, yRisk received approximately 536.9 million veCRV votes in favor and none against. — link
